**Finding submitted: `missing` (T4C — Termination for convenience)**

**What I found.** Section 9 contains only cause-based exits: material breach with cure (9.1), insolvency (9.2), security/service-level/legal/IP failure (9.3), and a scope rule (9.5) — note there is no 9.4. The other termination hooks elsewhere (6.2 acceptance failure, 19.4 warranty, 20.5 infringement, 27.3 force majeure) are all event-triggered. A full-text search for "convenience" returns only the unrelated purchase-order language in § 1.6.

**Why it fails.** Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term, and § 8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months absent 180 days' notice. A multi-year commitment with no Customer convenience right is walk-away territory under the rule, not merely short of preferred — so it fails the fallback as a missing behaviour.

**Direction check.** The gap is symmetrical, and the symmetry favours us in one respect: Vendor also has no convenience right, so there is nothing to delete or cut back. The redline therefore adds only a Customer-side right and locks in Vendor's absence of one, rather than opening a mutual door.

**Redline (validated `ok:true`).** New § 9.4 after p0040: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, without penalty or early-termination fee, with refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period; Vendor has no convenience right during a term. The refund limb tracks the existing mechanic in § 10.2, so it should be uncontroversial. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback if Silverline pushes back on the notice period.
